clients.name: VS Code
clients.notes: The checked-in extension scaffold and syntax-only TextMate grammar are package-checked, and the installed VS Code Linux x86_64 lane exercises activation, shared-LSP projections, commands, and the bounded keyboard workflow; macOS/Windows, publication, and broader accessibility remain unclaimed.

clients.name: VSCodium
clients.notes: Uses the same checked-in extension scaffold, TextMate grammar, and generated VSIX as VS Code; the installed VSCodium Linux x86_64 lane exercises activation, shared-LSP projections, commands, and the bounded keyboard workflow; macOS/Windows and publication remain unclaimed.

clients.name: Neovim
clients.notes: Checked-in native runtimepath setup is exercised in installed Linux x86_64 Neovim 0.10.4 and 0.12.5 hosts, including the bounded keyboard workflow; no distribution package or macOS/Windows claim.

clients.name: Zed
clients.notes: The checked-in extension manifest, pinned grammar/query projection, static task argv, and API-0.7.0 LSP launcher have partial installed Zed 1.18.1 Linux x86_64 evidence, including LSP requests, syntax rendering, task status/termination, and keyboard navigation; non-BMP, stale-version, rename-edit, macOS/Windows, and gallery claims remain unmade.

artifacts.notes: The extension source, TextMate grammar, and package manifest are checked in. A deterministic VSIX containing the grammar is generated and package-checked, but the archive is ignored build output rather than a checked-in artifact.
The source package is checked by scripts/check-zed.sh and installed as a local development extension by scripts/check-zed-host.sh; no gallery artifact or publication is claimed.

distributions.notes: Publication is not implied by a future VSIX build.
Open VSX availability is tracked separately from VS Marketplace.
The source runtimepath package is the primary distribution artifact; its Tree-sitter grammar is a supporting artifact. No plugin-manager-specific distribution is required by the contract.
Local development-extension install is exercised on Linux; gallery packaging, signing, and publication remain owned by #192.
